source: Biganzoli-Rangel et al. 2023, PLoS ONE 18: e0285271, Fig. 1: majority-rule tree from a partitioned Bayesian analysis; rectangular, root left, tips right, thin lines, posterior-probability dots at nodes, collapsed clades drawn as open triangles, coloured clade bands and a legend box; bats (Chiroptera: Emballonuridae). Image: the journal's figure image ('large' size from journals.plos.org, unmodified).

names_note: no matrix held; list = the printed tip names (see gold_note for renamed duplicates)
gold_note: Emballonurid bat tree, 31 tips, fully resolved; several tips are collapsed clades drawn as triangles and keep their printed names. 'Peropteryx macrotis' is printed four times; the gold numbers them _1 to _4 from top to bottom. The Rhynchonycteris naso samples keep their printed qualifiers without brackets (Rhynchonycteris_naso_11_Belize, _Panama, _Belize). Outside-corpus case: chosen to test whether the tool generalises beyond dinosaur figures, not drawn at random. Topology transcribed from the figure and checked node by node; topology only.
